Mr. Pawan Mishra, learned counsel for the appellant.
2. Mr. Deepak Bisht, learned DAG for the State.

3. This is an appeal filed by the appellant/convict against the judgment and order dated 16/19.02.2024 passed by the Special Judge, (POCSO)/Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Dehradun,
whereby the appellant/convict has been convicted and sentenced to undergo three years rigorous imprisonment under Section 363 IPC along with fine of Rs.10,000/- and the appellant/convict has also been convicted and sentenced to undergo ten years rigorous imprisonment under Section 376 IPC along with fine of Rs.10,000/-.
4.

entities.text: Special Judge, (POCSO)/Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Dehradun
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Also heard on the bail application (IA No.1 of 2024).

5. Learned counsel for the appellant/convict would submit that the victim was major at the time of alleged incident and the relation was consensual between the victim and appellant/convict; that, the victim has turned hostile during the trial itself and did not support the case of the prosecution; that,
the appellant/convict was on bail during trial and he has never misused the liberty of bail granted to him.
6.
Learned counsel for the State opposed the bail application, however would admit that the victim has turned hostile.

7. Having considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties but without expressing any opinion about the final merits of the case, the appellant/convict is admitted to bail on furnishing bail bond with two sureties in the amount of 40,000/- and personal bond of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned.
